# Teaching Principles {.unnumbered}

\lettrine{I}{n} conventional machine learning, data is passive and computational cost is paid in cloud kilowatt-hours. Datasets are scraped from the internet, curated, partitioned into training and validation splits, and treated as an exogenous ground truth ($x \sim P_{\text{data}}$). A vision classifier or language model inspects this data from behind glass; its predictions have no physical momentum and no causal power to alter the distribution of the documents it will encounter tomorrow. If a classifier mispredicts a label, the error is isolated—the physical world remains completely unaffected.

In Physical AI, this assumption collapses entirely. The data distribution of a physical machine is **endogenous**: the machine participates in a closed causal loop where every motor command changes the configuration of the physical plant, directly dictating what its sensors will observe next ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$).

::: {#pri-endogenous-data .callout-principle title="The Endogenous Data Invariant"}

**Invariant**: In embodied systems, actions alter the physical world and dictate future sensory inputs ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$). Under pure imitation learning with per-step error $\epsilon$, compounding covariate shift induces trajectory divergence growing quadratically with execution horizon $T$:
$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T |s_t - s_t^*|\right] = \mathcal{O}\bigl(T^2 \epsilon\bigr) $$
Because small execution errors compound into novel out-of-distribution states never seen in demonstration data, an embodied agent inevitably drifts off its demonstration manifold.

**Implication**: Training physical policies requires explicit architectural coverage of recovery trajectories. Teleoperation pipelines must log the Four-Stream Action Tap Tuple (human intent, policy proposal, supervisor intervention, plant feedback) to ensure the training distribution contains active corrections that steer the machine back to safety.

:::

Physical actions are not discrete tokens; they are continuous forces, velocities, and torques applied to physical mass.

::: {#pri-continuous-trajectory .callout-principle title="The Continuous Trajectory Mandate"}

**Invariant**: Discretizing multi-DoF continuous actions into discrete token vocabularies creates an intractable trade-off between quantization error ($\Delta a = (a_{\text{max}} - a_{\text{min}})/B$) and autoregressive decoding latency ($L_{\text{tokens}} \cdot \tau_{\text{step}}$). Furthermore, unimodal regression (MSE) collapses multimodal human demonstration distributions into catastrophic intermediate averages:
$$ a_{\text{MSE}} = \mathbb{E}[a \mid s] \notin \mathcal{A}_{\text{valid}} $$
where $a_{\text{MSE}}$ commands an unphysical collision path straight through an obstacle that the human demonstrated navigating around on the left and right.

**Implication**: Physical AI requires expressive continuous generative policies (Action Chunking with Transformers or Trajectory Diffusion Policies) that synthesize full continuous trajectory splines $A_{t:t+H} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times D}$, preserving multimodal demonstration modes while amortizing neural inference latency over multi-step execution horizons.

:::

Because open-loop accuracy metrics on static validation sets do not measure closed-loop physical survival, validation requires a new mathematical standard.

::: {#pri-butler-finelli .callout-principle title="The Butler–Finelli Exposure Law"}

**Invariant**: For ultra-reliable physical systems requiring a catastrophic failure rate $\lambda$ (such as $\lambda \le 10^{-7}$ critical failures per hour), validating that reliability with confidence $C$ solely through testing requires failure-free operational exposure time [@butler1993infeasibility]:
$$ T_{\text{test}} \ge \frac{1}{\lambda} \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - C}\right) $$
Validating $10^{-7}$ failures/hour at $95\%$ confidence requires over 30 million hours of failure-free physical operation—an empirical impossibility for any physical fleet.

**Implication**: Offline test-set accuracy and brute-force road mileage cannot validate physical AI safety. Dependability must be established through formal qualification ladders, non-asymptotic Clopper–Pearson coverage bounds, Extreme Value Theory tail extrapolation, and deterministic runtime containment rather than empirical optimism.

:::

Because the policy creates its own future sensory inputs, training an embodied model is not an exercise in curve-fitting; it is the deliberate management of **latent failure debts**:

* **Data as Physical Experience (@sec-data):** Every demonstration collected in the physical world consumes mechanical life—wearing cycloidal gearboxes, draining battery energy, heating motor stators, and accumulating sensor calibration drift. We examine the systems physics of bilateral teleoperation, multi-camera SerDes timestamp synchronization, and the Four-Stream Action Tap Tuple. We prove why logging human recovery interventions is mathematically required to prevent compounding covariate drift ($O(T^2 \epsilon)$) and keep the machine on its demonstration manifold.
* **Policy Training and Latent Debts (@sec-training):** Formulating policy architectures that can generate high-dimensional continuous trajectories without suffering mode collapse. We analyze the fundamental policy synthesis trade-offs across Behavioral Cloning, Offline RL, and Sim-to-Real RL. We explain why naive Mean Squared Error (MSE) fails on multimodal human actions (averaging two valid paths into an obstacle) and why Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) and Diffusion Policies succeed by predicting continuous trajectory splines. Crucially, we decompose the sim-to-real reality gap into friction hysteresis, structural compliance, and motor phase lag.
* **Evaluation as Closed-Loop Reality (@sec-evaluation):** Confronting why offline test-set accuracy is fundamentally decoupled from physical survival. A policy achieving $99\%$ open-loop accuracy on a static validation set can fail within seconds when closed in a real feedback loop due to non-Lipschitz sensitivity and compounding error. We establish the rigorous systems discipline of closed-loop evaluation—deriving non-asymptotic Clopper-Pearson coverage bounds, Butler & Finelli exposure limits, and Extreme Value Theory to evaluate tail-risk safety.

Part II teaches students how to curate physical data, train generative action policies, and measure closed-loop survival without falling into the trap of superficial benchmark optimism.
